CAR T-CELL THERAPY

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
FDA approved 30 August 2017.
This treatment is the collecting, reprogramming and multification of a patients’ own immune cells to treat their cancer.
The CAR on the cell’s surface is composed of fragments of synthetic antibodies. These receptors recognized and binds to the antigen on the tumor cell.
More than 80% of children diagnosed with ALL that arises in B cells will be cured by intensive chemotherapy. But for patients whose cancers return after chemotherapy or other traditional cancer treatment there are no options.
Of the first 59 children and young adults treated during the human trial period since 2012, 55 (94%) had a complete response, meaning their cancer disappeared.
Human trial started at CHOP in 2012 already and this approval of the therapy is a huge and dramatic development in cancer treatment and can be the beginning of many more similar treatments for other types of cancer as well.
Mia Cara is at CHOP now and is undergoing strong chemotherapy today, 17 Jan ’18, and on Friday to get the cancer count down before her T-cell treatment. And she is also treated with steroids.
The reason why she has not yet received her treatment: As part of their immune-related duties, T cells release cytokines, chemical messengers that help to stimulate and direct the immune response. It can lead to CRS (cytokine release syndrome). In the case of CRS, there is a rapid and massive release of cytokines into the bloodstream, which can lead to dangerously high fevers and precipitous drops in blood pressure. It is treated with steroids and immunoglobulin therapy, which provides them with the necessary antibodies to fight off infections. In her case she is not yet strong enough to withstand the high volumes of cytokines.
Anything can happen between now and February. She might be strong enough by next week to undergo the treatment! The doctors have not given up on her and are positive and working on getting her strong enough to get the treatment!

At the moment there is no hope for Mia Cara other than this treatment! Even if the worst happens before the treatment, this gave hope where there was none before and gives hope to other children in her position!

Press Release:


Car-T Cell Therapy
A South African family was devastated when their daughter was diagnosed with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia. Since her diagnosis three years ago, 6-year-old Mia Cara has undergone months of intense chemotherapy, lumber punches, gruelling bone marrow biopsies, intramuscular injections and countless days and nights in and out of hospital. But in a major medical breakthrough in genetics, US scientists have developed a specialized gene therapy treatment, which uses the body’s own immune system to treat Leukaemia in children. This treatment was recently approved by the FDA and hundreds of children have been successfully treated worldwide. After undergoing the Car-T cell treatment, Mia Cara is now officially in remission. Carte Blanche follows her remarkable success story.


Script:


CAR T THERAPY
Commission: 5161

AUDIO DUR
SUMIEN:
It’s huge. It is words you really don’t want to hear. Everything changes in an instant.
V/O:
For this young family from Somerset West, Sumien and José Ferreira and their two daughters, life as they knew it, changed overnight in August 2014 when Sumien took Mia Cara their firstborn, to the doctor.
12
SUMIEN:
I asked the doctor to do blood tests because we noticed a bruise on her hip. When I was bathing her, I saw a bruise this big on her hip.
V/O:
Mia Cara was diagnosed with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia, or ALL.
4
LINK:
ALL is the most common cancer in children and involves the B Lymphocytes which are responsible for the immune system.
7
V/O:
Following her diagnosis, Mia Cara underwent months of intense chemotherapy, lumber punches and bone marrow biopsies, intramuscular injections and countless days and nights in and out of hospital.
12
SUMINE:
It was the big unknown and the whole treatment was actually worse than you can imagine.
V/O:
Initially she responded well to the treatments but when she relapsed in May 2017, the family was devastated.
6
SUMIEN:
When a child relapses the whole protocol changes because the initial chemo treatment did not work, so they have to look at other options. She had seven blocks of chemo and then there is an option for a bone marrow transplant or for radiation. And with radiation on a little kid like that it has an impact on their mental development. That was basically the options given to us.
LINK:
The idea of radiation terrified Sumien and José and although they started with the donor bone marrow search, they were running out of time and were looking at alternative options.

8
V/O:
American scientists have been working on a new, less invasive treatment for cancer for the last 30 years and in August 2017, the US Food and Drug Administration approved a ground-breaking gene therapy for cancer, called CAR-T Therapy for treatment of children with ALL.

16
DR GRUPP:
This was going in front of the FDA, not only with a new medication, but with a new class of medications. Nothing like this had ever been approved by the Food and Drug Administration.
V/O:
Dr Stephan Grupp is Director of the Immunotherapy Program at CHOP, Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and has worked on human trials for this ground-breaking therapy since 2012.

It was during these trials that Emily Whitehead, who was running out of options to treat her aggressive, relapsed leukaemia, became the first paediatric patient to receive the treatment.
10


10
DR GRUPP:
We had a young lady in front of us, Emily Whitehead, whose cancer was not responding to anything. So, we have given her the most intensive chemotherapy that we had, and her bone marrow which is where the leukaemia lives, was completely full of leukaemia cells. People do not survive this, there is nothing you can do under those circumstances.
V/O:
Only three weeks after the therapy she was in remission.
4
DR GRUPP:
Really the clinical trial opened at the moment that she needed it. If it had been two or three weeks later, it would have been too late for Emily.
V/O:
Hearing about the CAR-T treatment, José applied to CHOP and Mia Cara was accepted into the programme.
7
DR GRUPP:
When Mia Cara’s parents were thinking of this particular treatment they were looking at it from a point of view of trying to avoid the long-term toxicities and problems associated with radiation.
V/O:
The first step in CAR T Therapy is to extract and separate a patient’s T Cells from their blood in a process called Apheresis, which is very similar to dialysis.

Dr Grupp, as Mia Cara’s doctor, performed this procedure with her in November last year.
11


6
DR GRUPP:
We have to make these cells for each individual patient because we are starting with their own cells. And T Cells are cells from the immune system that we want to genetically engineer.
V/O:
The T Cells are then taken to the lab.
3
DR JUNE:
And it is ten days of growing in the laboratory.

V/O:
Dr Carl June and his team developed the CAR T therapy in his laboratory at the University of Pennsylvania. CAR is considered the backbone of this therapy.

It’s an abbreviation for Chimeric Antigen Receptor, which means a foreign molecule is added into the DNA of the T Cell, using an inactive virus.

This procedure turns an ordinary T Cell into a killer T Cell that targets and kills cancerous B Cells.
10


16


12
DR JUNE:
When our CAR T Cell goes in – it has this lock-and-key mechanism. It will only bind with a cell that has CD19.
V/O:
The human CD19 antigen is a type of protein found on the surface of mature B Cells. These include cancerous as well as normal B Cells. CAR T Cells are genetically modified and programmed to recognize and latch onto any cell expressing CD19.
14
DR JUNE:
And when it does that, then basically within minutes it kills the tumour cell.
V/O:
The loss of normal B Cells in the process is regarded as acceptable collateral damage and is treatable.
6
DR JUNE:
It is a violent thing, of how the T Cell wanders and then boom! The Leukaemia cell is dead! But different to other drugs is two things. It can move on to another leukaemia cell and kill it. That is why it has been called serial killer cells. One CAR cell can kill many leukaemia cells and at the same time they divide and make more cells.


LINK:
That is the magic of this treatment! The cells do not have to be grown excessively in the lab, they keep multiplying and working in the human body!
10
DR JUNE:
So the patient becomes its own bio-reactor. And in fact, our first patients that we treated in 2010, we now have data that they still have these CAR T Cells on patrol in the patient.
V/O:
The genetically modified and reprogrammed cells are frozen until the patient is ready for the infusion and then transferred intravenously in just a few minutes.

Mia Cara had a second relapse in late December last year, days before she was supposed to have her infusion in Philadelphia.
9


8
SUMIEN:
They gave her six times the strength of chemo they previously gave her.
V/O:
But finally, between the massive chemotherapy treatments, the family found a window of opportunity to fly out to Philadelphia in January. Mia Cara received the infusion of her own engineered T Cells on the thirteenth of February this year.

The nearly three years since Mia Cara was diagnosed have been filled with pain for her and her family. More than ever, Sumien has become acutely aware of life's unpredictable nature.

14


11
SUMIEN:
Every time you put your child to bed could be the last time. I was sharing my bed with my two children here in Philadelphia, the one was lying on the one side and the other was lying on the other side. And just to have them with me was such an absolute blessing.
V/O:
The Ferreiras returned to South Africa with the amazing news that there is no trace of leukaemia in Mia Cara’s little body! She is officially in remission and the joy of this family knows no bounds!
14
LINK:
It seems that the team at CHOP now has an addition to the more than two hundred patients with B Cell ALL that they have successfully treated since the human trials started in 2012. And it started with Emily Whitehead, the very first paediatric patient to receive the treatment!


16
DR JUNE:
We did not know if it was a fluke. You know, when you treat someone… we did not know if it would last one day or ten days. Well she is now from 2012 to 2018… she is still in remission. And we found out that it is reproducible, so eighty to ninety percent of the children that we treat go into remission. So, it turned out to be much more potent than we anticipated.

PROMO’S

10 sec (1)
In a major medical breakthrough in genetics, the FDA has approved the use of a specialized gene therapy treatment, which uses the body’s own immune system to treat Leukaemia in children. (10)

10 sec (2)
Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia can be a devastating diagnosis for children, but a new FDA approved gene therapy treatment in the USA, is saving hundreds of lives worldwide. (10)


15 sec (1)
A young South African leukaemia patient successfully receives ground-breaking gene therapy to fight Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia in children. (7)

Dr June:
Eighty to ninety percent of the children that we treat go into remission. So, it turned out to be much more potent than we anticipated. (8)

15 sec (2)
How did scientists in the USA develop a life-saving gene therapy treatment to fight Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia in children? (7)

Dr Grupp:
We have to make these cells for each individual patient because we are starting with their own cells. (7)


15 sec (3)
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved a ground-breaking gene therapy treatment for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia in children. (8)

Dr Grupp:
This was going in front of the FDA with a new class of medications. Nothing like this had ever been approved by the Food and Drug Administration. (9)
